As Jangmi lifts north-northwestward, showers continue to build 
across the converging monsoon and trade-wind patterns. Latest model 
and satellite trends indicate intermittent breaks in showers activity
across the Marianas due to the disorganized pattern. Still, outflow 
boundaries from the nearby monsoon pattern and a nocturnal boost in 
showers may still bring an increase in showers overnight. Locally 
heavy showers remain possible through Thursday and isolated 
thunderstorms persist through Thursday night for Tinian and Saipan 
and through Friday or Friday night for Guam and Rota. Over the 
weekend, showers are expected to trend down to isolated as the 
trailing convergence from Jangmi shifts off to the west. However, an 
unsettled pattern remains nearby across western Micronesia, possibly 
bringing a slight uptick in showers across Guam and Rota.

Marine/Surf...
Moderate southeasterly winds will diminish back down to light to 
moderate starting Thursday. Combined seas of 5 to 7 feet are 
comprised of easterly trade swell and longer-period northerly swell. 
Southwest swell is expected to fill in over the next few days, 
building seas to 6 to 8 feet by Thursday night. There will be a 
moderate risk of rip currents along north and east facing reefs of 
the Marianas through the weekend. A low rip risk along south and west
facing reefs increases to moderate Thursday as a southwest swell 
builds into the region. There remains some uncertainty on the 
magnitude of the southwest swell. The GFSwave shows it building up to
6 feet, but this is dependent on the development of Jangmi and the 
monsoon pattern in western Micronesia.

Tropical Systems...
A tropical disturbance known as JTWC Invest 99W, has been upgraded 
to Tropical Depression Jangmi (06W) and has shifted northward to 
9.9N 137.3E, approximately 61 miles west-northwest of Yap Proper,
and remains entrenched in a developing monsoon pattern, with 
moderate to strong monsoon southwesterlies along the southern half
of the disturbance. Maximum sustained winds are estimated at 23 
to 26 kts. Dense cloud cover and deep convection remains along the
southern periphery, with shower bands condensing along the 
western side of the circulation. Over the next few days, Jangmi 
continues to lift north-northwestward, with a developing monsoon 
tail forming on the south side.

For more information on Tropical Depression Jangmi (06W), see 
bulletins issued by JTWC under WMO header ABPW10 PGTW and WTPN31 
PGTW and from the National Weather Service under WMO header WTPQ31
PGUM.

Eastern Micronesia...
Visible satellite imagery depicts the interaction between an ITCZ 
fragment and surface trough north of Pohnpei and Kosrae extending 
southeast, ending just south of Majuro. This interaction has remained
quasi-stationary, producing a northwest-to-southeast band of 
numerous showers and isolated thunderstorms affecting most of the
region. This primary weather maker will continue its weakening 
trend while remaining concentrated over Kosrae, so scattered showers
are expected to continue for the region overnight. A trade-wind 
trough north of Majuro is curving to the southwest and is expected to
merge with the leading edge of a developing ITCZ from the central 
Pacific. As a result of the ITCZ intensifying and propagating into 
the region, PoPs for Majuro are forecasted to peak on Friday. As time
progresses, model guidance will provide more clarity on this 
feature, so the intensity of showers for the region is all dependent 
on the timing and movement of the ITCZ within the coming days. As for
now, scattered showers and slight chances of thunderstorms are 
possible for all three forecast areas over the weekend.

Overall sea state remains steady with combined seas of 4 to 6 feet 
across Pohnpei and Kosrae and up to 7 feet near Majuro. Light to 
gentle easterly winds prevail across the entire region. Gusts will be
stronger near thunderstorms within coastal waters. The primary swell
is coming from an east to northeast direction fueled by the trade
winds and distant weather features in the mid-latitudes. A secondary
northerly swell is also expected to remain in the region through the
weekend. Early next week, seas may gradually subside as the easterly
and northerly swells potentially weaken.

Western Micronesia...
A tropical disturbance, formerly known as JTWC's Invest 99W has been
upgraded to a Tropical Depression 06W (Jangmi), and is currently 
centered near 9.9N 137.3E, about 61 miles west-northwest of Yap 
Proper. Numerous to widespread showers and isolated thunderstorms 
are seen along the southern, and western peripheries of Jangmi. Heavy
rainfall and gusty winds are expected across much of Palau and 
western Yap State, including Yap Proper this week. Westerly to 
southwesterly winds of 20 to 30 kt with gusts peaking near 40 kt are 
to be expected. This will cause seas hazardous to small craft and 
hazardous surf. A large band of heavy showers are occurring over
